title: Where Were We?
novel:
Marshall was [[devastated|devastate]] after Lily left for San Francisco. Every morning he [[stared|stare]] at the empty side of the bed, his heart [[aching|ache]] like an old [[wound|wound]]. Ted and Robin had become a couple, and everywhere Marshall looked, he saw [[romance|romance]] he could not have.

Barney decided the best [[remedy|remedy]] for a broken heart was a [[strip|strip]] club. "Nothing [[cures|cure]] sadness like [[distraction|distraction]]," he [[declared|declare]]. He [[dragged|drag]] Marshall to every [[entertainment|entertainment]] venue in the city, believing that [[naked|naked]] [[enthusiasm|enthusiasm]] would fix everything.

Meanwhile, Ted discovered that living with a [[heartbroken|heartbroken]] roommate was like sharing a room with a [[ghost|ghost]]. Marshall left [[pathetic|pathetic]] notes around the apartment: "Gone to find my [[dignity|dignity]."

Robin tried to [[comfort|comfort]] Ted. "He needs time," she said. But Barney had other plans. He took Marshall to a [[casino|casino]], a [[comedy|comedy]] club, and finally introduced him to a woman named [[Chloe|Chloe]]. For a [[fleeting|fleet]] moment, Marshall almost smiled.

But when he came home that night, he found one of Lily's old [[sweaters|sweater]] under the pillow. He [[held|hold]] it to his face and [[wept|weep]]. Some wounds, Ted [[realized|realize]], needed more than [[distraction|distraction]] to heal.

devastate.en: to make someone feel very shocked and upset

stare.en: to look at something for a long time without moving

ache.en: to feel a continuous pain that is unpleasant but not very strong

wound.en: an injury to part of your body or feelings

romance.en: a love story; the feeling of being in love

remedy.en: a way of dealing with a problem or curing an illness

strip.en: a place where dancers remove their clothes to entertain

cure.en: to make someone healthy again after an illness

distraction.en: something that takes your attention away from what you're doing

declare.en: to say something officially or in a confident way

drag.en: to pull something or someone with difficulty

entertainment.en: shows, music, films etc. that people enjoy watching

enthusiasm.en: a strong feeling of excitement and interest

heartbroken.en: very sad because someone you love has left you

ghost.en: the spirit of a dead person; someone who seems barely present

pathetic.en: making you feel pity or sadness

dignity.en: a calm and serious quality that earns respect

comfort.en: to make someone feel less sad or worried

casino.en: a place where people go to gamble

comedy.en: entertainment that is funny and makes people laugh

fleeting.en: lasting for only a very short time

sweater.en: a warm piece of clothing worn on the upper body

hold.en: to have something in your hand or arms

weep.en: to cry, especially because you feel very sad

realize.en: to understand a fact or situation, sometimes suddenly
